title: From one vector to a transformer block
summary: Sequence-to-sequence, attention, self-attention, and where embeddings sit.

choices.text: A token embedding is a fixed random vector per vocabulary entry. Only the layers above it are trained, which is why similar tokens do not end up near each other.

Attention lets each decoder step take a weighted sum of encoder states. The weights come from a score between the decoder's query and the encoder keys, so different output steps can look at different input positions.
A basic sequence-to-sequence model encodes the input into a single vector and decodes the output one step at a time from that vector. The fixed vector is a bottleneck on long inputs.
Self-attention needs a recurrent step to pass information along the sequence, because the weights at one position cannot depend on positions that come later.
Self-attention is a 1×1 convolution over the sequence, so one position cannot read any other; positional encodings are what let tokens mix.

An encoder block in a transformer is multi-head self-attention, a position-wise feedforward network, residual connections, and layer normalization. Positional encodings are added to the token embeddings because self-attention does not see order on its own.
